newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey buys 2.34 mln tonnes of wheat from farmers.
newsitem.headline: Turkey buys 2.34 mln tonnes of wheat from farmers.

text.p: Turkey's state grain board (TMO) has bought 2.237 million tonnes of wheat and 1.45 million tonnes of barley from farmers so far in the 1997/98 harvest season, Agriculture Minister Mustafa Tasar said on Tuesday.
He said this compared to 492,000 tonnes of wheat and 500,000 tonnes of barley in the previous harvest year.
"There is a 500 percent rise in the TMO's purchases as of August 1," he said in a statement.

TMO, the government's grain purchasing agent, has changed its policy of avoiding grain buying in large amounts which gave farmers the opportunity to trade with middlemen. But this led to fluctuations in local wheat prices and surging imports, forcing the government to buy more grain and later sell it locally to control prices.
The government also raised import tax rates twice in the past six weeks on wheat, barley and corn to raise imported grain prices to the local levels and divert grain processors to domestic crop.
Tasar said the government had paid 133 trillion lira to farmers for grain, fertiliser subsidies and other incentives as well as repaying debts from previous years.
Turkey is expected to produce about 16 to 17 million tonnes of wheat and seven million tonnes of barley this year.
